audit-targets: none

The refutation target does not survive as written. The delivery tip can remain the durable source of candidate work, but it cannot alone distinguish a live claim from an abandoned claim or establish GitHub merge/issue state. No separate queue database is implied by that distinction.

I confirmed HEAD equals 072f52daa393493556507f6ca203908a42e7cb21, used SHA-pinned source reads, and read only issue comments through 5783842686. The panel-deposit matches that ceiling. Source checks reproduced the stated Tracking evidence-map/default-evidence gap and the warnings-only clean-result path. Those diagnoses stand.

## Ref creation and stale reclamation do not provide exclusive ownership
blocks-the-design
Evidence: In an isolated OS-temp Git repository with a bare local remote, I pushed HEAD to refs/heads/swarm/finalize/4919 twice. The first returned exit 0, new branch; the second returned exit 0, Everything up-to-date. I then exercised the proposed no-open-PR window: deleting that ref and recreating it both returned exit 0. No project remote was mutated. At the dispatch SHA, finalize-cohort.ts pushAndOpenPr uses ordinary git push, and the existing swarm occupancy code has owner/session checks, but those local checks do not supply cross-machine ownership of this proposed remote ref.
Failure mode: Two maintainers starting from the same delivery tip can both interpret a successful push as ownership. Even if acquisition becomes atomic create-only, caller B can see A's newly created branch before A opens its PR, classify it as stale, and delete it while A is still working. Both callers are authorized maintainers, so the proposed ruleset does not distinguish them. A rejected push can also mean authorization or transport failure, not an incumbent owner.
Disposition: Before bind, specify atomic absent-ref acquisition with an unambiguous winner, distinguish errors from contention, and replace no-open-PR-implies-stale with an ownership/recovery protocol that cannot reclaim a live preparer. Reclamation and subsequent writes need fencing against a replacement owner. A ref may carry the necessary coordination state, but it is state outside the delivery tip. Add an interleaving test that pauses A after claim and runs B through discovery/reclamation before A resumes; the ordinary two-completed-runs test misses this race.

## Sequential calls retain the previous story's branch
blocks-the-design
Evidence: SHA-pinned finalize-cohort.ts:612-671 shows syncBaseBranch merges origin/base into the current checkout with --ff-only, and ensureFeatureBranch returns the existing feature branch when one is already checked out. Lines 1176-1186 invoke those helpers before each sweep; lines 684 and 718 stage all xbrief changes and push the selected branch. I ran source assertions confirming the existing-current-branch return path. The proposed loop names one detached worktree and sequential finalize-cohort calls, but no per-story branch reset.
Failure mode: After story A opens its leftover PR, the shared worktree is on A's branch with A's completion commit. Story B's call retains A's branch. If the delivery tip has not advanced, B can append its completion to A's PR; if it advanced incompatibly, the ff-only sync can fail. Claiming remote branch B does not change the worktree's current branch. This violates one leftover PR per story and may alter a PR after auto-merge has been enabled.
Disposition: Before bind, require each iteration to start from an explicitly selected clean delivery snapshot on its own claimed branch, and ensure the finalizer uses that branch rather than silently retaining another one. Reusing one worktree is viable with this explicit transition. Test two owed stories while A's leftover PR remains open, verifying separate branches and that B's PR excludes A's completion.

## Candidate discovery is not proof of human merge or actionable state
sharpens-framing
Evidence: SHA-pinned fetchPrDeliverySnapshot checks merged_at, base.ref, and merge_commit_sha; verifyDeliveryAncestry checks delivery ancestry. These checks do not establish that the merger was human. closeOriginsAfterLeftoverComplete separately reads live issue state and protected labels. Proposal items 6-7 additionally distinguish open/conflicted PRs and remote claims, none of which the active-brief field encodes.
Failure mode: Calling the field proof of a human merge encourages session-start and label readers to promote author-written metadata into verified action authority. The same delivery tree can have an open or closed issue, an absent or live claim, and a clean or conflicted leftover PR. A fetch-only tree scan cannot produce those distinct states.
Disposition: The candidate predicate can bind if described as discovery only. Preserve the existing validated delivery snapshot as action authority, state which live reads supply session-start classifications, and give unavailable reads an unknown outcome. Keep identity validation and command argument binding at the boundary. This needs precise separation of candidate data, validated delivery, and coordination state, not a replacement queue store.

audit-targets: none

The refutation target does not survive. An active brief on the delivery tip whose `plan.metadata.productPullRequest` is set is a candidate index. It is not, by itself, a story a human merged, and `swarm:finalize-owed` and mutation session start cannot act from that one predicate with nothing else stored.

## Active file leaves the tip before the issue closes
blocks-the-design
Evidence: At `072f52daa393493556507f6ca203908a42e7cb21`, `git ls-tree -r --name-only -- xbrief/active` prints only `xbrief/active/.gitkeep`. `git grep productPullRequest` at that SHA is empty. Product merge `e3c48c684` (pull request #4909, `merged_at` 2026-09-22T17:52:50Z, base `master`) adds `xbrief/active/2026-09-22-4907-bugtest-windows-release-step-5-dies-on-symlink-and-illegal-f.xbrief.json`. At that blob, `plan.status` is `running`, the only reference is `x-xbrief/github-issue` for deftai/directive#4907, plan items have `title` / `status` / `id`, and metadata has no pull-request field. Leftover merge `eec15b57b` (pull request #4913, `merged_at` 2026-09-22T18:15:51Z) renames that path to `xbrief/completed/`. Issue #4907 `closed_at` is 2026-09-22T18:18:23Z. The same gap is on #4906: leftover #4914 `merged_at` 2026-09-22T19:03:32Z (`b6425115e` renames active to completed) and the issue `closed_at` is 2026-09-22T19:05:58Z. `closeOriginsAfterLeftoverComplete` records a warning when the completed path is absent from `origin/<deliveryBranch>` (`packages/core/src/swarm/finalize-cohort.ts` 501-511). The caller sets `ok` from an empty error list (1056-1075), and `buildResponse` prints `FINALIZE CLEAN` when `ok` is true (1410-1411). The REST close is a later PATCH in that function (563-564), after the completed file is on the tip. `xbrief/completed` at this SHA is 1602 paths. `plan.metadata.completionProvenance.prNumber` is written on the completed brief (`packages/core/src/scope/delivery-evidence.ts` 325-329), which is the file that exists only after the rename.
Failure mode: Bound as written, the owed predicate becomes false when the leftover rename lands, while the issue is still open. Both commands, acting from that one predicate, skip the story. That is the measured window on #4907 and #4906, and it is the state the proposal calls close-owed. Close-owed needs the completed file, the absence of the active twin, and a live open issue. The open bit is not on the tip.
Disposition: The bound sentence names both tip shapes. The open/closed bit is a REST read of that issue before any close, and that read keeps `isProtectedStayingOpenUmbrella` (`finalize-cohort.ts` 450-457). A gate that scans only an active file with the field stays silent in the window these two merges already produced.

## The integer is not the delivery snapshot
sharpens-framing
Evidence: `fetchPrDeliverySnapshot` (`finalize-cohort.ts` 165-168 and 894-926) requires `merged_at`, `base.ref` equal to the delivery branch, and `merge_commit_sha`, then `verifyDeliveryAncestry` (`packages/core/src/scope/delivery-evidence.ts` 243-313) fetches `origin/<deliveryBranch>` and requires that commit to be an ancestor of the tip. `evidenceByIssue.set` runs only for issues returned by `fetchClosingIssues` (`finalize-cohort.ts` 936-942). `defaultEvidence` is set only when `validatedPrs.length === 1 && evidenceByIssue.size > 0` (1167-1168), so one Tracking pull request does not become delivery. Ancestor is true for every older merge commit still reachable from the tip. `.github/workflows/branch-gate.yml` 44-70 runs `task pr:check-closing-keywords` on `pull_request` with `contents: read` and `pull-requests: read`. `deft-story` does not occur in `*.ts` or `*.yml` at this SHA.
Failure mode: Session start blocks, and the owed command opens a leftover and enables squash auto-merge on the operator credential, from the author integer alone. The proposal's own item 6 says the snapshot inside finalize is the merge check. A rejected snapshot leaves the field set, so every later mutation session stays blocked. An integer that names any reachable older merge passes the ancestor check and is recorded as delivery for the wrong pull request.
Disposition: The field selects a candidate. `fetchPrDeliverySnapshot` and ancestry still have to accept it before a block, a leftover, an auto-merge, or a close. A rejected candidate has an explicit outcome that removes the block. The bound sentence describes a candidate index plus that existing snapshot. It drops the claim that the field alone means a human merged, and the claim that nothing else is stored.

## The lock ref is not the branch finalize already pushes
sharpens-framing
Evidence: `deriveLabel` (`finalize-cohort.ts` 586-600) uses an explicit label, otherwise `pr-<pull numbers>`. The branch is `swarm/finalize/${deriveLabel}` (1180). `ensureFeatureBranch` (656-671) keeps the current branch when `symbolic-ref` succeeds, and creates the requested name when HEAD is detached or branch policy exits 1. `pushAndOpenPr` (718-772) pushes that branch and opens the pull request. `safeSegment` (77-102) keeps digits, so an issue-id label becomes `swarm/finalize/<N>`. The proposal's lock is a separate push of `swarm/finalize/<N>`, and its stale rule deletes that ref when it has no open pull request.
Failure mode: With no label, the leftover pull request is on `swarm/finalize/pr-<M>`. The lock ref `<N>` has no pull request, so the next run treats `<N>` as stale, deletes it, and re-derives while the `pr-<M>` pull request is still open. A second leftover follows. The sentence "nothing else stored" also removes the lock the two-maintainer acceptance line uses.
Disposition: One ref, the branch `pushAndOpenPr` pushes, created with a create-only push. Stale deletes that same ref. The tip can remain the candidate set. The lock is stored state, and the bound sentence says so.

## The issue id is a same-repository tuple the caller currently drops
sharpens-framing
Evidence: `extractIssueRef` (`packages/core/src/capacity/backfill.ts` 66-99) returns the `owner/repo` tuple and the issue number from a `github-issue` URI. `finalize-cohort.ts` 1153 keeps the number and drops the tuple. The 4907 brief at `e3c48c684` also stores `plan.metadata.issueBody` and `plan.metadata.issueCommentThread`, which are copies of the issue thread, beside the typed reference. The proposal's push workflow has `issues: write` and takes N from the brief. The owed command then runs `swarm:finalize-cohort --pr M --stories N` and can REST-close N.
Failure mode: A brief that a human merged can name another repository's issue number, or a number that appears only inside the copied thread. The label workflow and the close apply that bare number in deftai/directive. A shell interpolation of `M` or `N` from JSON takes whatever string the field holds. The operator credential then opens and auto-merges the leftover, and the workflow's `GITHUB_TOKEN` labels the issue.
Disposition: Take N only from `extractIssueRef`, and require the tuple to equal this repository before a label, a ref, a finalize argument, or a close. Pass M and N as integer argv. Read `plan.metadata.productPullRequest` as a JSON number. Leave `issueBody` and `issueCommentThread` unread for this scan.

## Session start cannot see a tip-only record on the current hot path
sharpens-framing
Evidence: Session postures are `read-only`, `mutation`, and `requirements` (`packages/core/src/session/session-start.ts` 137). Optional network is off unless `--with-network` or `DEFT_SESSION_START_NETWORK=1` (216-222, 516-523). Re-arm skips that network (224-227). Turning the flag on also runs the release probe and the triage cache hydrate (324-330, 1981). `yolo-standing` occurs in `content/contracts/design-critique.md` and does not occur under `packages/**/*.ts`. The proposal's failed fetch prints one repository line, `finalize owed: unknown`, and does not list stories. The two exits it names are `swarm:finalize-owed` and `--defer-owed`.
Failure mode: A failed fetch starts the mutation session with an empty owed list, which is the dropped record. A successful `git fetch origin <deliveryBranch>` in the operator git directory moves the shared remote-tracking ref under every worktree of that repository, including a worker inside `verifyDeliveryAncestry`. `yolo-standing: yes` is a critique-comment token. Pointing session start at it runs the owed command (push, leftover, squash auto-merge on the operator credential, issue close) and then continues.
Disposition: Keep this fetch off `allowOptionalNetwork`. Write it to a private ref. A failed fetch is its own recorded exit, in the same family as a deferral, and the session does not start with an empty list. Session start does not read `yolo-standing`. An automatic owed run needs a product policy field whose default is off.

The road not taken is a side database of owed pull requests. The tip can stay the candidate set: the brief is already there after the product merge, as `e3c48c684` shows. That reading stops at the rename, at the second ref, and at the snapshot. It would flip if the bound sentence had both tip shapes, the live issue read, the existing snapshot as a required accept, and one create-only ref equal to the branch finalize pushes.

audit-targets: none

Refutation charter, round 1, ceiling 5783842686. Reads pinned with `git show 072f52daa393493556507f6ca203908a42e7cb21:`; `git rev-parse HEAD` matches the dispatch SHA. Thread read: 5783825531 and 5783842686 only.

The triage's four diagnosis anchors re-run clean, so I did not spend findings on them. `evidenceByIssue.set` is reached only from `fetchClosingIssues` (`packages/core/src/swarm/finalize-cohort.ts:936-942`); `defaultEvidence` is gated on `validatedPrs.length === 1 && evidenceByIssue.size > 0` (`:1167`); `ok = errors.length === 0` (`:1275`) with `closeOriginsAfterLeftoverComplete` taking the `warnings.push` arm when the completed brief is not on origin (`:500-508`), and `FINALIZE CLEAN` printed at `:1411`; `.github/workflows/branch-gate.yml` `closing-keywords` runs `pr:check-closing-keywords` and nothing else. One anchor is stronger than the body claims and is worth saying out loud: the merge and ancestry validation at `:886-925` (`fetchPrDeliverySnapshot`, the `snap.prBase !== deliveryBranch` refusal, the `snap.mergeCommitSha` refusal, `verifyDeliveryAncestry`) runs and pushes `validatedPrs` **before** `fetchClosingIssues` is ever called. Item 1 is therefore a small change over an already-independent check, and item 6's "Finalize's own merge and ancestry validation is the check that PR M merged" is accurate for the command. It is not accurate for the gate, which is finding 2.

## The claim ref and the leftover pull request branch are different refs, so every claim reads stale
blocks-the-design
Evidence: item 6 claims a story by pushing `swarm/finalize/<N>` and then calls `swarm:finalize-cohort --pr M --stories N`. That namespace is already occupied. `finalize-cohort.ts:1180` builds the branch as `swarm/finalize/` plus `deriveLabel(args.label, prNumbers, storyTokens)`, and `deriveLabel` (`:586-601`) returns `safeSegment("pr-" + prNumbers.join("-"))` whenever `--label` is absent and `--pr` is present — the story-token arm is only reached with no `--pr`. `pushAndOpenPr(projectRoot, branch, ...)` at `:1241-1250` pushes that branch and opens the leftover pull request from it. With `--pr M --stories N` and no `--label`, the leftover pull request's head ref is `swarm/finalize/pr-M`. `content/skills/deft-directive-swarm/references/core-phase-5-6.md:269` documents the same namespace for the existing sweep path.
Failure mode: `swarm/finalize/<N>` never acquires an open pull request, because the pull request is opened from `swarm/finalize/pr-M`. Item 6's stale rule is "a branch `swarm/finalize/<N>` with no open pull request, or whose pull request is conflicted, while the story is still owed, is stale. The command deletes the branch and re-derives from the current tip." So on the very next run — including a second maintainer's concurrent run — every claimed-and-still-owed story is classified stale, its claim ref is deleted, and the work is redone beside the live leftover pull request. Acceptance criteria 9 and 10 both fail as written: the second run reports stale, not in flight, and produces a second leftover pull request. Criterion 10 also never exercises a real stale case, because the non-stale case is unreachable.
Disposition: before bind, item 6 must state which ref carries the claim and which carries the work, and the stale predicate must read the ref the pull request is actually opened from. Passing `--label <N>` collapses the two names but does not fix the race (finding 7); it makes the claim ref and the work branch the same ref, so the claim is consumed by the work rather than outliving it.

## The session-start gate blocks on a field nothing has verified, and no run can clear a bad one
blocks-the-design
Evidence: item 7 says "On a successful fetch, the same scan as item 6 runs" — the scan, not finalize. The scan predicate is `plan.metadata.productPullRequest` set and no completed twin on the tip. The merge check lives in `finalize-cohort.ts:886-925` and requires `--repo`, a REST `fetchPrDeliverySnapshot`, and `verifyDeliveryAncestry`; none of it runs in the scan. `git grep productPullRequest` at the dispatch SHA returns nothing, so the field is new and hand-authored ("The author writes that field on the branch before merge", item 3).
Failure mode: an active brief on the tip whose `productPullRequest` names a pull request that did not merge into the delivery branch — wrong number, a closed pull request, a base that is not `deliveryBranch` — is permanently **owed**. Item 7 makes owed block mutation session start for every maintainer on every machine. `swarm:finalize-owed` cannot clear it: finalize's own validation is what refuses, so the story stays owed and the block stays. The design names no un-owe path. The only remaining exits are `--defer-owed <reason>` on every session forever, or a hand edit of a brief on the delivery branch — the hand step this issue exists to remove, now global instead of per-story.
Disposition: before bind, either the scan carries enough verification to refuse a bad binding rather than block on it (in which case "one predicate with nothing else stored" is no longer the remedy), or an owed story that finalize refuses degrades to a listed non-blocking anomaly, the way item 6's active-with-completed-twin anomaly already does.

## The gate's first exit needs the session the gate is blocking
blocks-the-design
Evidence: item 6 opens with "One command, run from any mutation session." Item 7 says owed, close-owed, and stale "block the start" and "The two exits are `task swarm:finalize-owed`, or `--defer-owed <reason>`". `packages/cli/src/session-start.ts:430` fixes the posture set as `read-only|mutation|requirements`, and item 7 has read-only and requirements skip the scan. The command pushes refs, runs the lifecycle commit, and opens pull requests, so it is mutation work by every definition this repository uses.
Failure mode: the maintainer who wants to clear the queue must start a mutation session to run the command, and the gate refuses that start until the queue is clear. The honest recovery is to record `--defer-owed` in order to get the session that then does the work, which writes a deferral into the session record of the session that did not defer. Item 7's stated purpose for that field — "so a deferral is a decision and not a lapse" — is inverted on the most common path.
Disposition: before bind, one of the two sentences has to move. Either `swarm:finalize-owed` is runnable outside a started mutation session and item 6 says so, or the gate offers finalize-owed as an in-gate action that completes before the start proceeds rather than as a shell command the operator is told to go run.

## "Nothing else stored" is not what the design does
sharpens-framing
Evidence: the same eight items store three other things. Item 6 pushes a remote ref per story and reads it back as both the lock and the stale input. Item 8 writes a `finalize-owed` label on issue N. Item 7 writes `--defer-owed <reason>` into the session record. The ref is not incidental: it is the entire concurrency control, and finding 1 is a defect in how it is read.
Failure mode: as a design sentence this is only wrong, not broken — but it is the sentence being bound, and it suppresses the questions the extra stores raise. Nothing in items 6 through 8 says what reconciles a claim ref, a label, or a deferral against a tip that has moved underneath them, because the framing says there is nothing to reconcile.
Disposition: the target's first clause should say that the owed *derivation* is the tip alone, and that claims, queue visibility, and deferrals are derived stores with their own staleness. The design survives that restatement; the sentence does not survive as written.

## The delivery tip is not a gated surface on this repository
sharpens-framing
Evidence: `branch-gate.yml` line 3 is `on: pull_request` with `types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, edited]`. It cannot observe a direct push. The five commits immediately before the dispatch SHA are direct pushes to master: `b7397ba38 chore(policy): allow direct commits for v0.119.7`, then `568783a0f chore(xbrief): move closed 4917 brief to completed`, `d24290491 chore(xbrief): mark 4917 brief completed`, `a9dc061a7 chore(xbrief): stamp 4917 complete transition`, `90501eb45 chore(release): v0.119.7`, and the dispatch SHA itself is `chore(policy): restore branch protection after v0.119.7`. 123 of the last 400 master commits carry no `(#N)` suffix, and roughly twenty of the last 300 commits touching `xbrief/active/` are direct (`19521dc64`, `b90bb8875`, `b76d41b0e`, `4084e3c5c`, `aa5f06aba`, and others). Protection-off release windows are a recorded, repeating operation, and moving briefs by direct commit inside them is the normal release lane.
Failure mode: item 3 is named as the enforcement behind the target's "is a story a human merged" inference, and it structurally does not run on the path the release lane uses. A brief carrying `productPullRequest` that reaches the tip during a protection-off window has had zero checks applied, and lands directly in finding 2's blocking scan. The three-commit 4917 transition also shows the tip is not atomic across a lifecycle move; a gate that fetches mid-transition reads an intermediate tip.
Disposition: state the direct-push window as an explicit precondition — either the release lane never writes `productPullRequest`, or the scan treats a brief whose introducing commit is not a merge as unverified rather than owed. Saying the closing-keywords job enforces the field is not true of this repository's master.

## Nothing checks the deletion of an active brief, and the tip is the only copy
sharpens-framing
Evidence: item 2 binds `deft-story: N` against "the `xbrief/active/` paths the pull request diff adds or changes relative to the merge base". Deletions are neither.
